QF.id: AIFM CII Legal Documents and Negotiations_5

question.text: A 'no-fault divorce' clause in the IMA of a Cat II AIF, as distinct from a 'for cause' removal clause, typically refers to:

answer.text: A clause permitting investors to replace the manager without establishing fraud, wilful misconduct or gross negligence, usually subject to a high consent threshold.
A clause allowing the manager to exit the fund voluntarily at no cost to LPs.
A clause waiving the manager's carry entitlement if a key-person event occurs.
A clause automatically terminating the AIF if SEBI cancels registration of any sponsor-group entity.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** 'No-fault divorce' is the investor's right to remove the manager WITHOUT having to prove events of default. It is the counterpart to 'for-cause' removal (which requires fraud/wilful misconduct/gross negligence). Because the manager is not at fault, no-fault divorce clauses typically carry a higher investor-consent threshold and an economic package (e.g., residual carry, transition fees). **The Trap:** Voluntary manager exit is a separate concept ('manager resignation'). Carry waiver on a key-person event is a key-person clause remedy, not divorce. SEBI registration cancellation is a regulatory event, not a negotiated LPA mechanism. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C covers the same removal taxonomy across all three categories. XXI-B Portfolio Manager does not have this LPA-style divorce concept because PMS contracts are bilateral client-PM agreements. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Negotiate the no-fault divorce threshold upward (often 75% by commitment) and include a graduated economic package: full carry on investments made pre-divorce, pro-rata on transition, zero on post-divorce. Keeps alignment intact even after removal.
